summary: Iteration 60: Full backend + frontend testing of the new Platform Super-Admin console at /admin. Ran 16 pytest cases (all passing after one selector fix in the test) covering admin auth, isolation, metrics, tenants, users, AI keys (list/PUT/empty-revert/live-probe), health, suspend/reactivate/reset-access, non-owner enforcement, suspended-user 403 enforcement in get_current_user, and tenant regressions. Frontend verified via Playwright: login screen, wrong-password error, successful login lands on admin-portal with admin-overview, all 4 primary metric cards populated with real numbers, AI Keys tab shows all 5 providers, Workspaces tab renders 27 tenant rows, Users tab shows suspend buttons (owners correctly excluded), Health tab shows database ok / scheduler running / emergent configured / providers env. No bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: admin.py test_all_keys probe is ~25-30s (real provider calls) - fine for admin-triggered, but the FE should show a spinner during the probe (already done via Test All Keys button state — verify UX).
admin_get_ai_keys never returns actual key material (only masked/source) which is correct; PUT accepts full key — good.
get_current_user suspended-check correctly returns 403 for tenant endpoints while admin cookie is unaffected — isolation confirmed.
Suspend endpoint correctly blocks owner (400) — verified. No potential to lock the entire tenant out.
Consider rate limiting /api/admin/ai-keys/status (25s probe) to prevent accidental DoS from repeated clicks.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file /app/backend/tests/test_iteration60_admin.py can be re-run as regression. Note /api/auth/me returns {user: {...}} not the user directly - remember when writing tenant tests. Admin session uses cookie dos_admin_token (requests.Session persists it automatically). AI key probe endpoint takes ~25-30s so tests use timeout=60 there. Anthropic status = 'out_of_credits' is expected (external billing).
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs found. Only one test-authoring mistake (expected /me to return user at top level) which was fixed in the test.
